notes:
Need searches first.I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 130, because I wasn't able to gather a single source.

My first try was to open the commentary pages directly: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, BibleHub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary) and the NET Bible notes. The tool rejected all six because it only opens pages that have first turned up in a search. When I then tried to run the searches, I'd hit the limit on tool calls for this turn, so nothing came back.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. With nothing read, anything I wrote would come from my own memory, so there's nothing reliable to give you yet.

If you ask again in a new message, I'll run the searches first and then open the pages they return. I'll cover:
- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** Reformed (Ligonier, Monergism, including John Owen's exposition of this psalm), Lutheran (LCMS and 1517 on Luther's reading of it), Baptist (Desiring God, GTY) and Wesleyan (wesley.nnu.edu, Seedbed).
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey for modern scholarship, and Catholic and Orthodox readings (New Advent, Catholic.com, OCA), where this psalm is known as the *De Profundis*.

That will give you verse-by-verse notes ("v. 4: ...") with a URL after every point.
